subject: general
question: A bike rider travels 30 kilometers at a velocity of 5 km/h and then comes back along the same path at 6 km/h. What is the cyclist's average speed for the entire trip?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** traveled is the **same** for both parts of the journey, the average speed is the **harmonic mean** of the speeds.

Average Speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) ÷ (s₁ + s₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 5 × 6) ÷ (5 + 6) = 60 ÷ 11

Average Speed ≈ 5.45 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5.45 km/h.**
